items.title: 6.4.1.3 Peer-to-Peer Network and Its Usage in Blockchain

source_refs.note: Topic 6.4.1.3 (PDF 163, printed 160). MCQ 16 and short question 1 are answered.

blocks.title: Peer-to-peer (P2P) network
blocks.text: A P2P network is one in which computers (nodes) communicate and share resources directly with each other without a central server; each node acts as both client and server.

In a file-sharing network, users download parts of a file directly from many other users' computers at once, which is faster and more efficient than one central server. In blockchain, nodes pass transactions and blocks directly to each other.

blocks.prompt: Analyze the role of P2P networks in blockchain (short question 1). What is their primary function (MCQ 16)?
blocks.explanation: (c) to enable direct data sharing between nodes without a central server. Every node receives and forwards new transactions and blocks, keeps a full copy of the ledger and checks blocks against the rules. Because there is no central server, there is no single point of failure or control, the network keeps working if some nodes fail, and the many copies make tampering detectable.

items: P2P: nodes share directly, each client and server; it is the backbone of blockchain.
